bib.title: LongRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Long-context LLMs

legacy_report:
SOURCE: LongRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Long-context LLMs. Ziyan Jiang, Xueguang Ma, Wenhu Chen (Univ. of Waterloo). arXiv 2406.15319v3, 1 Sep 2024 (preprint, no venue printed). Filename says 2024.

COVERAGE: 60,017 of 60,017 chars read (all 19 pages: body, appendix A.1-A.4, references skimmed). Figures 3 and 4 are image-only, so their curves were not read; only the captions and prose were. Extraction was clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Grouping short docs into ~4K-token retrieval units shrinks the NQ corpus about 30x and raises top-1 answer recall by about 20 points.
  number: 22M to 600K units; AR@1 52.24 to 71.69
  setup: NQ, Wikipedia Dec 2018. Retriever is bge-large-en-v1.5 via Tevatron. Passage (~120 tokens) vs grouped docs (avg ~6K tokens, grouped by hyperlinks). Answer recall at the unit level.
  quote: "Employing a long-context retriever (with an average number of tokens for each retrieval unit up to 6K) compresses the corpus size by up to 30 times (from 22M to 600K), enhancing top-1 answer recall by approximately 20 points (from 52.24 to 71.69)."
  where: Table 2 caption, p.6
- Eight grouped-document units match 100 passages on recall, which is about 10x fewer units.
  number: grouped k=8 AR 88.53 on 50K test-set tokens; passage k=100 AR 89.92 on 14K tokens; passage k=200 AR 91.30
  setup: NQ, same as above
  quote: "8 retrieval units at the grouped document level can achieve similar recall as 100 retrieval units at the passage level."
  where: p.7 (Table 2 rows)
- HotpotQA shows the same effect. Document-level k=2 gives R 30.01 and AR 47.75. Grouped k=2 gives R 56.30 and AR 72.49. Grouped k=8 gives R 74.71, close to document k=100 at R 74.84.
  number: corpus 5.2M to 500K
  setup: HotpotQA fullwiki dev set, abstracts only, so no passage level is tested.
  quote: "Grouped Documents 500K 2 1K 8K 56.30 72.49" and "Document 5.2M 2 130 200 30.01 47.75"
  where: Table 3, p.7
- Recall is not the same as end quality, and short units cost accuracy. Past a turning point, more units hurt the reader. The best reader context is about 30K tokens. The turning point falls at 100-200 units for passages, 5-10 for documents and 4-8 for grouped documents. Passage-level recall@200 is 91% but end performance dips from hard negatives.
  number: 91% (recall@200); ~30K tokens; the turning-point ranges above
  setup: NQ and HotpotQA, 200 test cases, 40K-token recall budget. The curves are in Fig 3 and were not read.
  quote: "In general, the most suitable context length fed into the reader is around 30K tokens."
  quote2: "the end performance does not increase monotonically with the recall score"
  where: p.2 (intro) and p.10 (3.5)
- Whole-document units beat many 200-token chunks on long-document QA.
  number: Qasper F1 22.6 (100 passages) vs 26.3 (1 doc). MultiFieldQA-en F1 51.3 (100 passages) vs 57.5 (5 docs). Abstract headline: 25.9 and 57.5, versus a previous 22.5 and 51.2.
  setup: Qasper (avg 4.7K tokens, 371 cases) and MultiFieldQA-en (6.9K, 150 cases). The authors refactored both from single-doc QA into retrieve-then-read tasks. Reader is GPT-4o. Compared with 200-token passages.
  quote: "On the Qasper dataset, gathering 100 short retrieval units of 200 tokens each into the reader achieves a 22.6% F1 score, while using a single long retrieval unit of 5K tokens achieves a 26.3% F1 score."
  where: 3.4, p.8
  Note: the abstract says 25.9 for Qasper, while the text and Table 6 say 26.3 for k=1 and 25.9 for k=2. This is an internal inconsistency to flag. Table 6 shows Qasper falls from 26.3 (k=1) to 21.6 (k=10), so more long units hurt.
- Embed a long unit as a max over small chunks (MaxP), not as one long vector.
  number: BGE-Large with 512-token chunks AR@1 71.7%; E5-Mistral-7B on 4000-token chunks 54.2%; E5-Mistral-7B on the whole grouped unit 23.4%
  setup: NQ grouped units (~6K tokens). sim(q,g) ≈ max over g′⊆g of E_Q(q)·E_C(g′), after Dai & Callan 2019.
  quote: "Using a general embedding model and approximating by maximizing the similarity scores between the query and all chunks within the retrieval unit is better than using the existing long embedding model to encode the entire context."
  where: Table 4, p.7
- End-to-end QA with no training and no reranker, top 4-8 units.
  number: NQ EM 62.7 (GPT-4o, 4 units), 58.6 (Gemini-1.5-Pro). HotpotQA EM 64.3 (GPT-4o, 8 units), 57.5 (Gemini). For comparison, Atlas is 64.0 on NQ, MDR is 62.3 on HotpotQA, and closed-book Claude-3-Opus is 49.2 on NQ.
  setup: the "refined EM" described below; baselines use standard EM.
  quote: "LongRAG (GPT-4o; Recall 4 units) 62.7" and "LongRAG (GPT-4o; Recall 8 units) 64.3"
  where: Table 5, p.8
- Rule for unit construction. Docs over ~4K tokens are kept whole. Docs under ~1K are grouped by relatedness (hyperlinks). Typical k is about 100+ for passages, about 10 for documents and 4-8 for grouped documents.
  number: 4K threshold; k values as stated
  setup: NQ-style Wikipedia.
  quote: "If the original document is already long (e.g., longer than 4K tokens), we treat the entire document as a single unit. If the original document is relatively short (e.g., shorter than 1K tokens), we group related documents together to form a single unit."
  where: 2.1, p.4
- Reader choice matters. On 200 NQ questions, GPT-4o is best at 62% (the figure text reads 59.5, 61.5, 62, 61, 60, 51 across the six readers; the label-to-model mapping is uncertain). DeepSeek-V2-Chat is clearly worse at 51%.
  quote: "Deepseek-V2-Chat is one of the best open-source LLMs, but its performance degrades significantly compared to the previous five black-box LLMs."
  where: Fig 4 and 3.5, p.10
- Two-turn reading works better on long context. Turn 1 uses no examples and gives a long answer. Turn 2 uses 8-shot extraction of a short answer.
  quote: "we empirically find that using a similar prompt as for short contexts, where the model extracts the final answer directly from the long context, often leads to decreased performance."
  where: 2.2 and A.1, pp.5 and 16

LIMITS
- The "refined EM" is more lenient than standard EM. A prediction counts if it is under 5 tokens and the ground truth is a substring of it, or the reverse. The authors say they checked it by hand. They only "believe" the difference is not significant for the baselines, so the comparison to Atlas and MDR is not strictly like for like.
- Unit-level ablations use only 200 test cases.
- Qasper and MultiFieldQA retrieval quality was not measured. They are not extractive tasks, so only end F1 is compared.
- Grouping relies on Wikipedia hyperlinks. The authors say any relatedness function would work, but only hyperlinks were tested.
- Long embedding models are weak (Table 4). Whole-unit encoding is the bottleneck, and the authors expect it to improve.
- The framework depends on proprietary long-context readers. Open-source DeepSeek-V2 falls well behind.
- No cost or latency is reported for 30K-token reads, and no head-to-head against a reranked top-k pipeline.
- Dated: the readers are GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro and Claude-3-Opus (2024), and the embedder is bge-large-en-v1.5. The 512-token encoder limit has since eased, since the related work mentions 32k embedding models.

BUILDS ON
- Chen et al., 2017 (DrQA), Lewis et al., 2020 (RAG) and Karpukhin et al., 2020 (DPR): 100-word passage units.
- Dai & Callan, 2019: MaxP scoring.
- Izacard & Grave, 2020b (FiD): top-100/200 passages plus a reranker.
- Xiong et al., 2020b (MDR) and Izacard et al., 2022 (Atlas): baselines.
- Xiao et al., 2023 (BGE), Gao et al., 2022 (Tevatron) and Johnson et al., 2019 (FAISS): retrieval tooling.
- Saad-Falcon et al., 2024 (LoCoV1): the design for refactoring Qasper and MultiFieldQA into RAG tasks.
- Bai et al., 2023 (LongBench): MultiFieldQA.
- Khalifa et al., 2022: the AR metric for HotpotQA.

CODE
- Algorithm 1, group documents (p.18). Sort D by degree ascending. For each d, find the groups containing any related doc r in adj[d]. Start g_new={d}. Sort those related groups by size. Merge each one while |g_new|+|g|<=S (S is the max tokens per group), removing the merged group from G. Add g_new to G.
- Similarity (p.4): sim(q,g) ≈ max_{g′⊆g} E_Q(q)^T E_C(g′). Aggregate: C_F = Concat(g1..gk).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): traditional RAG vs LongRAG pipeline. Long retriever and long reader, no ranker.
- Fig 2 (p.4): hyperlink grouping, shown on a multi-hop HotpotQA example.
- Fig 3 (p.9): unit size and number of units vs EM, and recall vs EM, for NQ and HotpotQA. Key for the "more recall is not better" point. Image-only and not read.
- Fig 4 (p.10): six readers on NQ.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The Fig 3 data is image-only. The Fig 4 label order is ambiguous. The abstract's Qasper 25.9 differs from the text's 26.3. The pypdf extraction merges some words in the abstract and the references. The reference list was skimmed only.
